skills.fallback: The pm skill rewrites the update itself with the ask first, outcomes against goals second and detail last, then rates it on the rubric in PM.md section 7.

steps: Write the asks first: each decision or kind of help needed, from whom, and by when
Report outcomes against goals in three to five lines, with numbers from the inputs
State the top risk and what you are doing about it
Cut activity that does not change a decision or a goal, and keep the cut material separately
Check every number against the inputs and mark the update DRAFT
outputs: an update of five to ten lines with the asks first
the cut material, kept separately in case someone asks
a score against the rubric
checks: the first line is an ask, or says there is no ask this time
every number matches its source
it stays under 250 words unless you set another limit
nothing was sent
setup: Claude Code with this repo, as a plugin or a clone
optional: Udi Menkes' Awesome PM Skills for exec-comms (/plugin marketplace add menkesu/awesome-pm-skills, then /plugin install awesome-pm-skills@awesome-pm-skills)
workflows.example_prompt: My draft monthly update to our VP is in updates/october.md and it runs to two pages. I need her to approve a contractor for the data migration. Rewrite it so she reads the ask.
limitations: it cannot know your leaders' preferences unless you tell it or record them in context/PRODUCT.md
it drafts, and you send
a short update hides detail, so keep the cut material ready

workflows.name: Decision memo when leaders disagree
workflows.problem: Two leaders want different things, such as the enterprise feature or the onboarding fix, and the decision is deferred meeting after meeting while the team waits.
inputs: the decision and the options on the table
each side's position, quoted wherever it is written down
the evidence for each option
who decides, and by when

skills.name: pm
skills.role: lays out the options fairly and checks the evidence

skills.name: decide
skills.role: turns the call into a one page memo with kill criteria and a review date
skills.fallback: The pm skill writes the memo itself from the decision brief template in PM.md section 5, adding kill criteria and a review date.

steps: State the decision in one sentence, with who makes it and by when
Write each option in the words its supporters would use, with its evidence and confidence
Write what each option costs: what it delays, what it risks and what it needs
Recommend one option, say what would reverse the recommendation, and set kill criteria and a review date
Check that each side would agree their option is described fairly, and mark the memo DRAFT
outputs: a one page decision memo
each option described in its supporters' terms, with evidence
what each option costs
a recommendation with kill criteria and a review date
checks: each option is described as its supporters would describe it
every piece of evidence cites its source
the memo names who decides and by when
the kill criteria are measurable
setup: Claude Code with this repo, as a plugin or a clone
optional: Udi Menkes' Awesome PM Skills for decide (/plugin marketplace add menkesu/awesome-pm-skills, then /plugin install awesome-pm-skills@awesome-pm-skills)
workflows.example_prompt: Our head of sales wants SSO and audit logs next quarter; our head of growth wants to fix onboarding. It has been deferred three times. Notes from both and the data we have are in decisions/q1/. Write the memo that gets it decided.
limitations: it can make the trade off clear but cannot make leaders agree
a fair description of each side needs their own words, so it asks for them rather than paraphrasing
the recommendation is yours to stand behind or change

workflows.name: Saying no with evidence
workflows.problem: A senior stakeholder or a large customer asks for something that does not fit the plan. Saying yes would displace work that matters more, and a bare no will damage the relationship.
inputs: the request, in the requester's words
the current plan, and what the request would displace
evidence: how many customers need it, usage data, the strategy
optional: what you could offer instead

skills.name: pm
skills.role: weighs the request against the plan and drafts the reply

steps: Restate the request as the need behind it, in the requester's words
Check the evidence for the need: how many customers have it, or how much revenue depends on it, from the inputs
Show what saying yes would displace, and what that would cost
Find what you can offer: a smaller version, a workaround, a later date with a condition, or an existing feature that already helps
Draft the reply: what you heard, the decision, the reason with its evidence, the alternative, and when you would look at it again
Mark the reply DRAFT and list the risks of sending it
outputs: a short analysis of the request against the plan
a draft reply with the reason and an alternative
what would change the answer
checks: the need is stated in the requester's words
the reason cites evidence, not opinion alone
the reply offers an alternative or says honestly that there is none
nothing was sent
setup: Claude Code with this repo, as a plugin or a clone
workflows.example_prompt: Our largest customer wants a custom reporting module by March, and it would push back the onboarding work for everyone else. Their email and our plan are in requests/. Help me say no in a way that keeps the relationship.
limitations: it drafts, and you decide whether the answer really is no
it cannot know commercial promises sales made unless you include them
a reply is not a relationship, and a call may land better than an email

workflows.name: One on one preparation
workflows.problem: A one on one with your manager or a key stakeholder is in half an hour. Open items are scattered across chat, documents and the tracker, and you will walk out without the decision you needed.
inputs: who the meeting is with and what they care about
open items since the last meeting: notes, threads, tickets
what you need from this meeting

skills.name: pm
skills.role: orders the agenda around what you need

skills.name: meeting-prep
skills.role: gathers open items and talking points from the tools you have connected
skills.fallback: The pm skill builds the agenda from the notes and items you paste in.

steps: Write the one thing you need to leave the meeting with
Gather the open items since the last meeting, and the status of everything you promised them
Order the agenda: your ask first, then their likely concerns, then updates
For the ask, write the evidence and the options in two or three lines
Write the questions you want to ask them
outputs: a one page agenda with your ask first
the status of your promises to them
the evidence for your ask
your questions
checks: the agenda starts with a specific ask, or says there is none
every promise listed cites where it was made
nothing is written about the other person that you did not provide
the agenda fits the length of the meeting
setup: Claude Code with this repo, as a plugin or a clone
optional: PM Pilot's pm-core plugin for meeting-prep (claude plugin marketplace add mshadmanrahman/pm-pilot, then claude plugin install pm-core@pm-pilot)
meeting-prep reads Jira, Slack, Calendar and Granola through connectors you add, so without them you paste the items in
for Jira, use Atlassian's own server from resources/README.md rather than the community server that PM Pilot's README links
workflows.example_prompt: I have a one on one with my director in 30 minutes. My notes from last time and this week's threads are in 1on1/. I need her to decide whether we pause the reporting work. Prep me.
limitations: notes about colleagues are sensitive, so keep them on your machine and out of shared repositories
it prepares you, and the conversation is yours
it cannot read tools you have not connected
